findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the deleteMany uses OR: [{method SMS, scheduledDate lte now}, {retryCount gt 1}]. The second OR branch has no method filter, so any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted by the SMS cron job. This causes unintended data loss for email/whatsapp reminders, which this SMS job should never touch; the retryCount predicate must be ANDed with method SMS (and scheduled:false).

findings.title: Missing phone number never increments retryCount causing infinite retry
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 158 the schedule attempt is guarded by if (message?.length && sendTo). If sendTo is falsy (e.g. invalid/missing phone number, the exact case in the PR description) or message is empty, the loop does nothing: no scheduled flag, no retryCount increment, no delete. The reminder stays unscheduled with retryCount 0 forever and is re-fetched every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, defeating the new retry limit and leaving the infinite scheduling loop the PR claims to fix.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount loses retries
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the failure paths do data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read at the start of the cron run, instead of an atomic increment. If the cron overlaps, is retried, or the row was updated since the findMany, concurrent writes overwrite each other and a failure is lost, so reminders can be retried more than the intended twice. Use Prisma atomic operation { increment: 1 }.
